The PDFs are not in the corpus, so their figures are cited, not quoted. Q3 FY2026 is not out yet; the deck URL returned 404 on 2026-11-01. Rivals: 15 pages added to outside.jsonl (PMA, Axel Springer, Publicis URD 2020, Permira, PE Hub, BetaKit, Awin ×2, Net Influencer on LTK, TechCrunch, Relevant Audience on YouTube, Adweek, Affiverse, Modern Retail, Hello Partner). Pages that block scripts (Business Wire, MediaPost, eMarketer, Momentum Works, cj.com, PitchBook) are paraphrased in ‘single quotes’ with the URL. impact.com figures come from impactcom strategy financials (self-reported). Every rival figure is the rival's own claim unless marked; none is audited except Rakuten's.
  • Core claim: The competitor map in impactcom mission forces §5 has shifted three ways. 1. The networks are consolidating, and the biggest one now runs on impact.com. Awin swallowed ShareASale (2025). Partnerize swallowed Pepperjam (2020). Rakuten Advertising rents impact.com's contracting, tracking and payments (Apr 2026). Publicis has said nothing about CJ's numbers since it put CJ under a 'strategic review' in 2019. 2. Rakuten rented because buying was off the table. Its overseas unit, which holds Rakuten Rewards and Rakuten Advertising, earned $51.8M of operating income on $2.1B revenue in FY2025. Rewards revenue fell ~5% in each of Q1 and Q2 2026. The group is selling securities (¥200bn, May 2026) to deleverage from Mobile. Buying impact.com at 5–8x ARR would cost ¥200–325bn (derived). That is one more year of asset sales for a non-core unit. 3. The growth threat is the platforms that own the checkout. YouTube (1.3M+ affiliate creators), Amazon (Creator Connections, plus Associates rate cuts of up to 50%), TikTok Shop (~$15B US GMV, 2025) and Shopify Collabs (free app) each bring their own tracking, payouts and creator pool. They need no partnership platform. On PMA numbers, US affiliate spend grows ~14% a year and impact.com's ARR ~20%, so it still gains share of a pool that is ~$14B in the US. It is best placed to grow as the brand's neutral ledger across those platforms, not as a better network.

2. Where Rakuten Advertising and Rakuten Rewards sit

Rakuten Rewards (ex-Ebates) and the overseas advertising business, i.e. Rakuten Advertising (ex-LinkShare, ex-Rakuten Marketing), sit inside Internet Services → International Business Unit → 'Open Commerce'. Per the deck footnote, Open Commerce is Rewards (US, Europe, Canada), Fillr and the 'overseas Ads business'. Rewards is the only one broken out. Rakuten Advertising has no revenue line of its own anywhere in the decks. PPC Land (outside) on Rakuten Marketing's history: it "acquired LinkShare in 2005 for $425 million in cash". (Context, not from Rakuten's IR: Ebates was bought in 2014 for about $1B.)

Period Rakuten Rewards revenue (¥bn, YoY) Rewards OI (¥bn, YoY) International BU revenue International BU OI Rakuten's comment
FY2025 149.2 (+2.7%) 7.6 (−26.4%) ¥314.3bn / USD 2.1bn (+2.4% in USD) ¥7.8bn / USD 51.8M Open Commerce revenue fell on ‘U.S. macroeconomic headwinds’ (FY25 release)
Q4/25 56.1 (+0.1%) 4.1 (−29.0%) ¥104.7bn ¥5.8bn Holiday quarter carries the year
Q1/26 26.6 (−4.8%) 1.4 (+196%) USD 459.2M USD 7.1M ‘sluggish revenue growth’ for Rewards. Collective Voice, Open Commerce's creator-marketing platform, ‘will be shut down’ (deck footnote)
Q2/26 31.5 (−5.2%) 1.8 (+11.6%) USD 499.7M USD 9.67M "Rakuten Rewards improved profit through the discontinuation of a low-margin service and effective cost control"

Read (derived): Rewards is ~11% of Internet Services revenue (149.2 / 1,369.7) at a ~5% operating margin. That is ~$1.0B of revenue at Rakuten's implied ¥150/$ (314.3 / 2.1). It is shrinking in 2026 and makes its profit from cost cuts. The headline 'advertising business' (¥65.6bn in Q2/26, +15.6%) is domestic ads on Ichiba and Travel. Rakuten's own footnote says ad revenue outside Japan sits in the International BU, so the growing ad line says nothing about Rakuten Advertising. Inference: Rakuten shut its own creator platform in the same quarter it signed with impact.com, whose bundle includes a creator product.

3. Balance-sheet pressure: why ally, not build or buy

Measure (Rakuten's figures) Value Date
Consolidated bonds and borrowings (ex-bank, card, securities lines) ¥1,754.9bn → ¥1,605.8bn Mar → Jun 2026
Rakuten Mobile loans, leases and others; of which owed to the parent ¥1,118.5bn; ¥803.7bn Jun 2026
Consolidated equity / total assets ¥1,318.2bn / ¥31,135.9bn (~4%, derived; mostly bank and securities balances) Jun 2026
Non-FinTech net interest-bearing debt / non-FinTech EBITDA 11.7x → 6.5x → 6.6x (6.2x before a temporary rise in point costs); target ≤5x within 2027 Dec-24 → Dec-25 → Jun-26
Bond redemptions 2026 USD perpetuals ¥81.7bn (Apr), JPY senior ¥20.0bn (Jun); 2026 funds 'already secured' Q2/26 deck
Asset monetisation Rakuten Bank overseas share sale (Dec 2023, now 49.27% held); 14.99% of Rakuten Card to Mizuho (Dec 2024); 19.99% + 29.0007% of Rakuten Securities to Mizuho Securities; ¥200bn sale of held securities (May 2026) Q2/26 deck footnotes
FinTech reorganisation Bank, Card and Securities HD merged into a Rakuten Bank Group from Oct 1 2026; ‘not intended for fundraising’, a net capital outflow for Rakuten; synergy target >¥85bn by FY to Mar 2030 Q2/26 CEO deck

Rakuten's stated policy (FY2025 release): "The Group will maintain a policy of securing funds for Rakuten Mobile for 2026 onwards primarily through self-funding." And in Q2: "In May 2026, Rakuten raised approximately 200 billion yen through the sale of held securities."

Build vs buy vs ally (inference, not stated by Rakuten). - Buy: impact.com at 5–8x ~$270M ARR (impactcom strategy financials §7) is $1.35–2.2B, or ¥200–325bn at ¥150/$. That is 1–1.6x the May 2026 securities sale and 2–3x the group's FY2025 Non-GAAP OI. It would sit on top of a non-FinTech leverage ratio Rakuten has promised to cut to 5x. The target would earn ~26–42x the International BU's whole FY2025 OI. - Build: rebuilding contracting, tracking and payouts in 60–70 currencies takes years of capex. Rakuten has ring-fenced capex for base stations (>¥200bn in 2026), in a unit whose OI is ~$50M a year. - Ally: costs little or no capital and keeps the override and the service relationship (the alliance says "Rakuten Advertising will continue to develop AI, analytics, automation and monitoring capabilities"). It turns technology capex into a vendor fee. Rewards also gets a second distribution channel at a time its revenue is falling.

The alliance is the only option that fits a deleveraging plan. The same logic means Rakuten is unlikely to bid for impact.com before 2027 unless the target is paid in stock (inference).

4. What Rakuten says about the alliance in its own IR

  • Nothing in the group's IR materials. The FY2025, Q1 and Q2 FY2026 releases and the Q4/25, Q1/26 and Q2/26 data and CEO decks do not mention impact.com (text search, 2026-11-01). The Q1 deck (May 14, two weeks after signing) does not mention the alliance either.
  • Announced one level down. The alliance came from the overseas subsidiary through PR Newswire on rakutenadvertising.com: "Rakuten International and impact.com today announced a strategic alliance". The 2026 English group press list we fetched (53 items) has no release on it.
  • Rakuten's framing is data, not cost: "Through Rakuten Rewards’ direct consumer signals, advertisers can better understand incrementality". No financial terms are given anywhere (impactcom strategy financials §6).
  • Inference: at group level the deal is immaterial (Open Commerce is a fraction of an International BU whose ¥7.8bn FY2025 OI is ~7% of group Non-GAAP OI, derived). For impact.com it is the largest channel deal it has. Each side's disclosure matches its own materiality.

YouTube Shopping affiliate Google Native product tags; retailers onboard via Shopify or networks (Awin runs the UK launch, context) "YouTube said more than 1.3 million creators are in the affiliate programme"; GMV 13x in two years; 35 countries by end-2026 The largest creator pool. impact.com is a partner via the YouTube Creator Partnerships API (2026), and so is its rival Awin

By model (inference). Network override players (CJ, Awin, Rakuten) sell publisher access and services; their weak spot is price, which impact.com already exploited. SaaS peers (Partnerize, PartnerStack, Everflow) sell the same rails and compete on vertical fit and price. Creator platforms (CreatorIQ, LTK) compete for a newer budget line that is often flat-fee, not CPA. Native platforms compete on the thing impact.com cannot own: the shopper, the checkout and the attribution data.

Retail's share of spend fell from 76% to 63%; finance, travel and telecom rose

APMA (UK) via Hello Partner £1.66bn UK spend — Trade body; same incentive as the PMA

Headwind inside the PMA study: 69% of publishers were "concerned about how recent Google actions, including algorithm changes and the advent of AI Overviews, are reducing site traffic and affiliate revenue". The supply side of the open-web channel is shrinking at the same time as the native platforms grow (inference).

Share arithmetic (inference). US spend grows ~11–14% a year; impact.com's ARR grows ~20%. The ~6–9 point gap is share gain from networks and in-house programs. Adding Rakuten's book is the next step-change. Beyond that, ARR growth falls back toward the pool's growth unless impact.com reaches budgets the PMA does not count: creator flat fees, B2B referral and AI-agent commerce.

8. What the claims don't prove

  1. Every rival number is a self-description. Awin's and CJ's 'revenue for advertisers' are attributed sales, not incremental sales. Neither page gives a year.
  2. Rakuten's segment data hides Rakuten Advertising. The decline in 'Open Commerce' could come from Rewards, Fillr or Advertising. Only Rewards is visible.
  3. No alliance economics anywhere. Rakuten's IR is silent, and impact.com's releases give no terms. Whether Rakuten pays impact.com per program or per transaction, or shares revenue, is unknown.
  4. Native-platform scale claims are unaudited: YouTube's 13x GMV, TikTok GMV from third-party trackers, Amazon's rate cuts from seven sources speaking to Adweek.
  5. Market-size sources have owners. The PMA is a members' body. eMarketer sits in the same group as Awin.

9. Strategic read (inference — not stated by impact.com or Rakuten)

  • The network-vs-SaaS war is over, and SaaS won the rails. The network side is consolidating (Awin+ShareASale, Partnerize+Pepperjam), going quiet (CJ inside Publicis) or renting (Rakuten). What is left to win there is execution: migrating Rakuten's advertisers without losing them to Partnerize, which offers SaaS plus services under one roof.
  • Rakuten's weakness is impact.com's opportunity and risk. A deleveraging parent with a shrinking Rewards line and a shut creator platform will keep the overseas unit capital-light. That makes impact.com the de facto technology owner of Rakuten's affiliate business. It also makes the business fragile if Rakuten later sells Rakuten Advertising to someone else, such as a PE roll-up or a holding company (speculative).
  • The real share fight is with the checkout owners. Amazon cutting Associates rates while growing brand-funded Creator Connections shows the pattern: the platform keeps the ledger and charges the brand. YouTube, TikTok and Shopify are each building the same thing. impact.com cannot beat them on the shopper. It can be the place where a brand contracts, pays, taxes and reconciles partners across them, as Trackonomics already does across networks (impactcom strategy financials §4).
  • Creator budgets are the biggest new pool, and they are contested. CreatorIQ (1,300+ customers) and LTK ($6B+ sales) are bigger in creators than impact.com's bundled Creator product. Rakuten exiting Collective Voice removes one rival. Bundling Creator free (Jan 2026) is a defensive price move, not a moat.

10. Canon lenses

  • Coopetition (canon brandenburger nalebuff coopetition): Rakuten is complementor and competitor at once. Awin is a rival network and also YouTube's UK onboarding partner, as impact.com is in the US.
  • Counter-positioning (canon helmer 7 powers): it worked against networks. Native platforms counter-position against impact.com in turn: free tools, funded by the checkout margin.
  • Disruption (canon christensen innovators dilemma): Shopify Collabs and the $30 tier are the low end. Amazon and TikTok are new-market entrants with their own value networks.
  • Multi-sided platforms (canon hagiu wright multi sided platforms, canon parker platform revolution): LTK and YouTube own the consumer side; impact.com owns the brand and partner sides only.
  • Five forces / where to play (canon porter competitive strategy, canon rumelt good strategy): the crux is supplier power of the demand gatekeepers (impactcom mission forces §4).
  • Platform hybrids (canon cusumano business of platforms): integrations (YouTube API, Shopify, MCP) are how a non-owner of demand stays relevant.

11. Practitioner counterpoint

  • For impact.com: every structural move of 2025–26 went its way. The #3 network rents its rails, the #2 swallowed the cheapest rival but kept the old fee model, and Amazon's cuts push publishers toward brand-direct programs. Growth of ~20% in a ~12–14% pool is share gain.
  • Against: the alliance has no disclosed economics, a counterparty under financial strain, and a group IR that does not mention it. Creator and native platforms grow faster than the PMA pool. impact.com is a guest on all of them.
  • Both: a neutral ledger across closed platforms is valuable only if brands run many platforms at once. That holds at enterprise scale, not for the Shopify SMB.

Open questions to track

  1. Rakuten Q3 FY2026 (mid-Nov 2026): Rewards revenue trend, and any first mention of impact.com in group IR.
  2. Alliance economics: fee basis, exclusivity, and who holds the advertiser contract.
  3. Does Publicis keep, sell or merge CJ? Any CJ number in a Publicis URD.
  4. Awin's ownership after the split (United Internet's 20%?) and any Awin figure in Axel Springer reporting.
  5. YouTube's and Amazon's next affiliate rule changes: do they route through networks and platforms, or around them?
  6. A primary global market-size estimate with a disclosed method.

Rep

Using only this note's numbers: (a) Convert a 5x, 6.5x and 8x ARR price for impact.com (~$270M ARR) into yen at ¥150/$. Express each as a multiple of (i) the May 2026 securities sale, (ii) FY2025 group Non-GAAP OI and (iii) FY2025 International BU OI (USD 51.8M). (b) Rakuten Rewards: compute the FY2025 operating margin and the H1 2026 revenue change against H1 2025. Back out H1 2025 from the YoY rates. (c) If US affiliate spend grows 11% and impact.com's ARR 20%, how many years until ARR doubles? How much does its share of the US pool rise over that time, assuming a fixed US mix?

Answers: (a) $1.35B = ¥203bn = 1.0x the sale, 1.9x group OI, 26x International BU OI. $1.76B = ¥263bn = 1.3x, 2.5x, 34x. $2.16B = ¥324bn = 1.6x, 3.0x, 42x. (b) 7.6 / 149.2 = 5.1%. H1 2026 = 26.6 + 31.5 = ¥58.1bn. H1 2025 ≈ 26.6/0.952 + 31.5/0.948 ≈ 27.9 + 33.2 = ¥61.2bn, so −5.0%. (c) ln2 / ln1.20 ≈ 3.8 years. The share rises by (1.20/1.11)^3.8 ≈ 1.34x, i.e. about a third more of the pool. That is share gain, but it is not a new market.
